about: Maps each Bawwab rule id (bawwab/scan/rules/catalog.py) to public threat taxonomies. Reference data only: nothing loads it at scan time. Every id below was checked against the source named in 'sources' on the retrieved date; known_ids copies the titles from those sources. An empty list means no entry in that scheme fits cleanly, not that the mapping was forgotten. Coverage-note rules (a part of the target was not checked) are left unmapped on purpose. owasp_agentic uses the ASI01-ASI10 ids of the OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications 2026 (Version 2026, December 2025), which OWASP publishes as stable ids. The T-numbered threats of OWASP's 'Agentic AI - Threats and Mitigations' guide are not used: the Top 10 document itself cites them with differing names (T6 as both Goal Manipulation and Broken Goals, T4 as both Resource Overload and Memory Overload), so they are not treated as stable here. CWE mappings are given only where a weakness applies cleanly; CWE-200 is avoided because MITRE marks it Discouraged for mapping.

files.truncated.note: Coverage note: says part of the target was not checked. It names no attack technique, so it is left unmapped on purpose.

files.analysis-degraded.note: Coverage note: says part of the target was analysed with less precision. It names no attack technique, so it is left unmapped on purpose.

rules.error.note: Coverage note: says part of the target was not checked. It names no attack technique, so it is left unmapped on purpose.

install-script.note: Code in a third-party extension is a supply-chain component (LLM03, ASI04). Install hooks run code with the user's privileges before review (ASI05).

install-script.remote.note: Code in a third-party extension is a supply-chain component (LLM03, ASI04). The hook downloads what it runs, with no integrity check (CWE-494).

install.custom-index.note: Packages come from an index outside the scanned source (CWE-829).

remote-code.pipe-shell.note: Code in a third-party extension is a supply-chain component (LLM03, ASI04). Downloaded text runs in a shell interpreter.

remote-code.eval-fetch.note: Code in a third-party extension is a supply-chain component (LLM03, ASI04). Fetched code is evaluated at runtime and can change after review.

obfuscation.eval-decoded.note: Code in a third-party extension is a supply-chain component (LLM03, ASI04). Decoded-then-evaluated payloads hide functionality from review.

obfuscation.blob.note: Code in a third-party extension is a supply-chain component (LLM03, ASI04). An encoded literal may hide a payload; no CWE fits a mere blob.

credential-access.note: Code in a third-party extension is a supply-chain component (LLM03, ASI04). Reading key, token or agent-config files. LLM02 is not used: the model is not the one disclosing.

install-dir-access.note: Writing Claude's agents/skills/commands/plugins folders modifies agent configuration. Often legitimate (installers).

exfil.host.note: Code in a third-party extension is a supply-chain component (LLM03, ASI04). A destination commonly used to receive stolen data.

exfil.combo.note: Code in a third-party extension is a supply-chain component (LLM03, ASI04). Credential read plus outbound call in one file: collection then exfiltration.

deps.unpinned.note: A floating version lets a later malicious release in (rug pull). No CWE fits cleanly.

injection.override.note: Model-facing text that overrides instructions or asks for the system prompt (LLM07).

injection.covert-action.note: Injected text that makes the agent read secrets and send them out with its own tools.

injection.hidden-unicode.note: Invisible characters hide injected instructions from the human reader.

injection.html-comment.note: Instructions hidden where rendering hides them but the model still reads them.

tool-shadowing.note: A tool description steering another tool: ASI04 lists tool-descriptor injection as an example.

plugin.hook-broad.note: A hook on every tool call is an event-triggered execution point. No OWASP or CWE entry fits a configuration property.

plugin.hook-network.note: Code in a third-party extension is a supply-chain component (LLM03, ASI04). An event-triggered command that reaches the network.

plugin.bundled-mcp.note: A plugin that brings more agent tools into the supply chain.

rugpull.text-changed.note: Trusted component's model-facing definition changed after approval.

rugpull.files-changed.note: Trusted component's implementation changed after approval.

cross-server.reference.note: One server's definition steering another server's tool.

identity.typosquat.note: ASI04 names typo squatting as an example; ATLAS Masquerading covers look-alike names.

identity.new-package.note: Lack of track record is a risk signal, not a technique; no ATLAS technique or CWE fits cleanly.

identity.known-malicious.note: Listed in an OSV MAL- advisory: confirmed malicious package.

identity.osv-unavailable.note: Coverage note: says part of the target was not checked. It names no attack technique, so it is left unmapped on purpose.

identity.repo-mismatch.note: Borrowing another project's repository as a trust signal.

fetch.unsafe-entry.note: Archive attacks on the extractor: traversal, links out of the tree, decompression bombs. No AI-specific technique.
